strings.d1.s0.name: Giza Pyramids
strings.d1.s0.tips: Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure. Arrive at the 07:00 opening for cool, quiet conditions. Entering the Great Pyramid costs an extra 1,500 EGP (narrow tunnel). Haggle camel rides to 200-300 EGP. Card payment only.
strings.d1.s1.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
strings.d1.s1.tips: Included with the pyramid ticket. Approach from the Valley Temple, where the morning light hits the face.
strings.d1.s2.name: Panorama Point Giza
strings.d1.s2.tips: A desert viewpoint that takes in all three pyramids at once: the classic photo.
strings.d1.s3.name: Khufu's Restaurant Giza
strings.d1.s3.tips: Modern Egyptian cuisine with pyramid views. Book ahead; 9 Pyramids Lounge is an alternative.
strings.d1.s4.name: Giza Sound and Light Show
strings.d1.s4.tips: A sound and light show in front of the Sphinx. Nights are cool; buy tickets in advance.
strings.d1.b0.name: 9 Pyramids Lounge
strings.d1.b0.tips: Lunch in the desert with pyramid views. Go here if Khufu's is full.
strings.d1.b1.name: Giza Camel Ride
strings.d1.b1.tips: 30 minutes on a camel in the desert. Fix the price beforehand.
strings.d2.s0.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: The vast museum opened in 2025. It holds Tutankhamun's complete treasure (5,000 pieces) and Khufu's solar boat. Book a timed ticket online (~1,450 EGP), allow 3-4 hours and take a morning slot.
strings.d2.s1.name: GEM Food Court
strings.d2.s1.tips: The eating area inside the museum, with pyramid views.
strings.d2.s2.name: Grand Egyptian Museum Garden and Obelisk
strings.d2.s2.tips: The hanging obelisk and the outer courtyard. Good for photos with the pyramid skyline.
strings.d2.s3.name: Koshary Abou Tarek
strings.d2.s3.tips: Cairo's most famous koshary (rice, lentils and pasta) since the 1950s. Downtown, four floors, 80 EGP.
strings.d2.b0.name: Zooba Downtown
strings.d2.b0.tips: Modern Egyptian street food: ta'meya and hawawshi.
strings.d2.b1.name: Egyptian Museum Tahrir
strings.d2.b1.tips: The old museum, home to the mummies and artefacts not moved to the GEM.
strings.d3.s0.name: Citadel of Saladin and Muhammad Ali Mosque
strings.d3.s0.tips: A fortress and an alabaster mosque. The terrace has views over Cairo and the pyramids.
strings.d3.s1.name: Sultan Hassan Mosque
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Mamluk masterpiece with a huge courtyard and a sense of calm.
strings.d3.s2.name: Al-Muizz Street
strings.d3.s2.tips: A Fatimid street of mosques, sabils (public fountains) and the Beit el-Suhaymi house, lit up at night.
strings.d3.s3.name: Naguib Mahfouz Cafe
strings.d3.s3.tips: Run by Oberoi inside Khan el-Khalili. Try the molokhia (jute leaf stew) and mint tea; air-conditioned.
strings.d3.s4.name: Khan el-Khalili
strings.d3.s4.tips: A 14th-century bazaar selling copper, spices and papyrus. Haggle down to a third of the first price. El Fishawy cafe is open 24 hours.
strings.d3.b0.name: El Fishawy Cafe
strings.d3.b0.tips: A mirrored cafe since 1773: mint tea and shisha.
strings.d3.b1.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
strings.d3.b1.tips: A mosque-university since 970. Go here instead of Sultan Hassan.
strings.d4.s0.name: Hanging Church
strings.d4.s0.tips: A 3rd-century church built over a Roman fortress, in Coptic Cairo. Take the metro to Mar Girgis.
strings.d4.s1.name: Coptic Museum
strings.d4.s1.tips: Coptic art and the Nag Hammadi texts.
strings.d4.s2.name: Ben Ezra Synagogue
strings.d4.s2.tips: Said to be where Moses was found. Home of the Cairo Geniza.
strings.d4.s3.name: Abou El Sid Zamalek
strings.d4.s3.tips: Egyptian food in 1920s-style decor in Zamalek. Try the stuffed pigeon and molokhia.
strings.d4.s4.name: Nile Felucca Ride
strings.d4.s4.tips: A one-hour sail on a felucca from Zamalek at sunset. Agree the price per boat.
strings.d4.b0.name: Sequoia Zamalek
strings.d4.b0.tips: A terrace on the Nile with shisha and meze. Go here instead of the felucca.
strings.d4.b1.name: Cairo Tower
strings.d4.b1.tips: A 187 m tower in Zamalek with city views.
strings.d5.s0.name: Saqqara Step Pyramid
strings.d5.s0.tips: The world's oldest pyramid (Djoser). The Serapeum, with its underground bull sarcophagi, costs an extra ticket. Cooler in the morning.
strings.d5.s1.name: Dahshur Red Pyramid
strings.d5.s1.tips: Entry inside the Red Pyramid is included (steep tunnel). The Bent Pyramid is next door and there are few tourists.
strings.d5.s2.name: Memphis Open Air Museum
strings.d5.s2.tips: The ancient capital, with a colossal statue of Ramses II and an alabaster sphinx.
strings.d5.s3.name: Saqqara Country Club Lunch
strings.d5.s3.tips: A farm restaurant among palm trees. Grills and Egyptian bread.
strings.d5.s4.name: Saqqara Carpet School
strings.d5.s4.tips: A hand-woven carpet workshop. No pressure to buy; just watch.
strings.d5.b0.name: Abou Shakra Giza
strings.d5.b0.tips: A kebab classic, for the way back.
strings.d5.b1.name: Bent Pyramid Dahshur
strings.d5.b1.tips: Inside the Bent Pyramid. Go here instead of the Red Pyramid.
strings.d6.s0.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
strings.d6.s0.tips: 2.5 hours from Cairo by train. A modern library and museums in a disc-shaped building.
strings.d6.s1.name: Qaitbay Citadel
strings.d6.s1.tips: A 15th-century fortress on the site of the ancient lighthouse, with Mediterranean views.
strings.d6.s2.name: Fish Market Restaurant Alexandria
strings.d6.s2.tips: Fish on the Corniche. Choose from the counter and eat with Mediterranean views.
strings.d6.s3.name: Kom El Shoqafa Catacombs
strings.d6.s3.tips: Roman-era underground tombs, a blend of Egyptian and Greek styles.
strings.d6.s4.name: Alexandria Corniche
strings.d6.s4.tips: Walk the seafront boulevard and take the tram to Montaza. Return train at 18:00.
strings.d6.b0.name: Mohamed Ahmed Foul Alexandria
strings.d6.b0.tips: Alexandria's classic for ful and falafel.
strings.d6.b1.name: Pompey's Pillar
strings.d6.b1.tips: A Roman column. Go here instead of the catacombs.
strings.d7.s0.name: Gezira Island Zamalek Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: The island neighbourhood: ivy-covered embassy streets and the Nile.
strings.d7.s1.name: Aisha Fahmy Palace
strings.d7.s1.tips: An art nouveau palace and gallery in Zamalek.
strings.d7.s2.name: Ovio Zamalek
strings.d7.s2.tips: Zamalek's breakfast and brunch cafe, for a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s3.name: Zamalek Nile Bank Last Tea
strings.d7.s3.tips: A last tea at a cafe with Nile views. The airport is 45 minutes away.
strings.d7.b0.name: Cairo Kitchen Zamalek
strings.d7.b0.tips: Home-style cooking. Go here instead of Ovio.
strings.d7.b1.name: Museum of Islamic Art Cairo
strings.d7.b1.tips: One of the world's best Islamic art collections. Go here instead of the Zamalek plans.
strings.note0: Uber and Careem are safe and cheap. You can't get taxi drivers to switch on the meter, so haggle. For Coptic Cairo, take Metro Line 1 (Mar Girgis). Giza is 1 hour away in traffic.
strings.note1: From June to September it is 38-42°C: visit the pyramids at 07:00, museums at midday and the Nile in the evening. Bring a hat and 3 litres of water.
strings.note2: Monument entrances take card only (2026), no cash. Book the GEM online with a timed ticket. Entering the Great Pyramid inside the Giza complex costs 1,500 EGP.
strings.note3: Koshary costs 50-80 EGP, ful and ta'meya 30, restaurants 300-600. Tipping (baksheesh) is expected everywhere: 20-50 EGP, or 10% in restaurants.
strings.note4: There are no 'free' photo or camel offers at the pyramids. Say 'la shukran' (no, thank you) and keep walking. Women should dress comfortably, with shoulders and knees covered.
strings.note5: In mosques, take off your shoes and women should cover their hair. Do not visit during Friday midday prayer.
